Maya Patel: FYI seeing ~18% lower prefix cache hit rate on Private vs Hosted for our 8k chat workload after the last runtime push. Repro on a small canary.
Conrad Li: how are you measuring hit rate? end-to-end or just KV store hits?
Maya Patel: KV store hits from netstore metrics + end-to-end observed token cost. KV hits dropped from ~72% to ~58% on Private. Hosted and Dedicated are still ~70%+.
Lee Wong: interesting. any config drift between Private and Dedicated? netstore path or mount options?
Maya Patel: yes. Private uses NFS mount through customer VPC, Dedicated uses internal blobstore. Suspect network latencies + small rekeys.
Sasha R: can you paste a sample cache key? might be normalization or tokenization mismatch.
Maya Patel: sample keys below (redacted):
```
prefix||sess_v1||md5:9f8a7b6c||model:gpt-small||len:512
prefix||sess_v1||md5:9f8a7b6c||model:gpt-small||len:512
```
Maya Patel: looks identical on face. but our profiler shows extra leading whitespace on private path sometimes.
Conrad Li: whitespace -> different hash -> miss. Does tokenization happen client-side or runtime-side?
Lee Wong: runtime does light normalization before hash. but there was a recent change to kernel selection where short-seq paths use a faster tokenizer shim for throughput. If Private falls back to a slower kernel for memory alignment we might be hitting a different normalization codepath.
Maya Patel: here's profiler snippet from runtime trace:
```
[kernel_selector] selected: aten_fast_attn for seq<=512 latency=1.2ms
[netstore] GET key=prefix||sess_v1||md5:9f8a7b6c latency=12ms
[kernel_selector] fallback: vectorized_token_norm for networked devices
```
Maya Patel: On Private the netstore GET jumps to ~25-40ms p95 (vs 3-8ms Hosted).
Sasha R: higher GET latency can change batching heuristics: runtime might reduce batching window to preserve latency SLO -> smaller batches -> different kernel chosen -> different tokenization path?
Conrad Li: exact. batching rules in runtime: if netstore_rtt > batch_threshold we shrink batch_sz by ~30% to keep 99th percentile token latency. That feeds into kernel selection which picks a different attention kernel optimized for smaller batch shapes.
Lee Wong: that kernel change triggers a different preprocessor path? we added an optimization that dedups trailing whitespace for aten_fast, but full tokenizer used for fallback kernels. that could explain key mismatch.
Maya Patel: so root cause might be config+latency -> batching -> kernel -> normalization divergence -> cache misses.
Conrad Li: do we have a reproducible trace where we toggle netstore latency? can simulate with tc qdisc on private canary.
Maya Patel: yes planning to run a net-emulation test tomorrow. will toggle 30-60ms delay, compare hit rates and kernel_selector logs.
Sasha R: also add a test that forces kernel selection to be identical across envs (env override) and see if hit rates converge.
Lee Wong: quick mitigation: make normalization deterministic and upstream before kernel-specific fastpaths. longer term: unify hashing step to happen before any kernel/normalizer branching.
Maya Patel: agreed. short-term patch: fall back to canonical normalization in netstore lookup if env==private. PR incoming.
Conrad Li: can you include perf counters in PR? want p95 netstore, kernel selection counts, batch size distribution.
Maya Patel: yes. CI will include a small perf harness.
